ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: During the Industrial Revolution, because of the production and deposition of large amounts of dust and soot around cities and factories, many insect species underwent significant changes. Researchers counted the numbers of spotted moths and long-tailed moths in 8 different urban environments within 1 square kilometer in 1802 and 1902, respectively. Which type of natural selection does this study reflect?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: During the Industrial Revolution, because of the production and deposition of large amounts of dust and soot around cities and factories, many insect species underwent significant changes. Researchers counted the numbers of spotted moths and long-tailed moths in 8 different urban environments within 1 square kilometer in 1802 and 1902, respectively. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The bar chart compares the number of moths detected per square kilometer in 1802 and 1902; the legend shows that black bars are 1802 and white bars are 1902. White-bodied spotted moths were about 35/km² in 1802 and decreased to about 6/km² by 1902; black-bodied spotted moths were about 8/km² in 1802 and increased to about 35/km² by 1902; long-tailed moths were about 36–37/km² in both counts, with very little change. Reasoning: Over 100 years, the spotted moth population did not show both extreme phenotypes increasing at the same time, nor was the intermediate phenotype retained; instead, it shifted from white-bodied individuals being dominant to black-bodied individuals being dominant. Combined with the fact that during the Industrial Revolution, dust and soot deposition around cities and factories made the environment darker, black individuals were less likely to be preyed upon and had a greater survival advantage, and the selection pressure continuously favored the direction of darker body color. Therefore, this reflects directional selection.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the two time points and compare each moth type’s counts. Note that over 100 years the pepper moth population shifts from mostly white-bodied to mostly black-bodied, rather than both extremes increasing or an intermediate being preserved. Then combine this with the text’s industrial soot context: darker environments make dark moths more advantageous. Since selection consistently favors one phenotype direction, conclude the study illustrates 定向选择.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：柱状图比较了1802年和1902年每平方公里检测到的蛾数量，图例显示黑色柱为1802年、白色柱为1902年。白体斑蛾在1802年约35只/km²，到1902年降到约6只/km²；黑体斑蛾在1802年约8只/km²，到1902年升到约35只/km²；长尾飞蛾两次统计都约36—37只/km²，变化很小。推理：100年间，斑蛾种群不是两端表型同时增加，也不是中间表型被保留，而是由白体占优势转向黑体占优势。结合工业革命期间城市和工厂周围灰尘、烟灰沉积使环境变暗，黑色个体更不易被捕食、更有生存优势，选择压力持续偏向较深体色这一方向。因此，这体现的是定向选择。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct visual-data-to-concept route: use the bar chart’s before/after phenotype frequencies and map the one-way shift in moth coloration to the definition of directional selection. Given the problem has one standard biological classification, this is the genuinely central method.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the bar chart: the legend shows black bars for 1802 and white bars for 1902; white-bodied pepper moths are high in 1802 but much lower in 1902, black-bodied pepper moths are low in 1802 but much higher in 1902, while longtail moths stay nearly unchanged.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text to establish the historical cause and study design: during the Industrial Revolution soot and dust accumulated around cities/factories, and researchers compared moth counts in 1802 versus 1902 across urban environments; the task asks for the type of natural selection.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the rule that directional selection occurs when environmental change favors one phenotypic extreme over the other, causing the population distribution/trait frequency to shift in one direction. Industrial melanism in peppered moths is the classic example: soot-darkened environments favor darker moths.
